locked_config.analysis_approach: Single global full-pattern fit via fit_pattern with SNIP background and auto peak detection. The dominant low-angle feature at ~3–4° is air-scatter/beamstop climb that would starve prominence-based detection (it is ~50–500× the real reflections) — exclude it by setting fit_range lower bound above the climb. Inspect where the steep climb flattens: it decays into flat background by ~5°, and the first genuine reflection sits at ~11° on flat background, so set lo ≈ 5.0°. Fit the full range 5–45°. Do not run a per-peak fit_profile loop; keep auto-detection so the recipe generalizes across the in-situ series frames.
locked_config.physical_model: Sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt profiles, one per Bragg reflection, on a SNIP background. eta (Gaussian-Lorentzian mixing) free per peak in [0,1]. Expected significant reflections (~7–9): ~11.0°, ~17.7°, ~18.6°, ~19.2° (weak), ~22.2°, ~26.0°, ~29.5°, plus weaker high-angle features. Peaks within 1.5×FWHM (the 17.7/18.6/19.2 cluster) fit jointly within the single global model.
parameters_to_extract: crystallite size via Scherrer (K=0.9) on 3-5 strongest isolated peaks
locked_config.fitting_strategy: 1) Set fit_range=(5.0, 45.0) to exclude the low-angle air-scatter climb (excluded channels dropped from background/detection/fit but returned as matched for residual diagnostics). 2) fit_pattern with method='snip' (snip_iterations='auto'), split pseudo-Voigt line shape, auto peak detection. 3) Check result: if only 1-2 peaks return with high R², lo is still inside the climb — raise it and re-fit. If a visible reflection (e.g. the ~19.2° shoulder or high-angle weak peaks) is missing from the residual as a peaked spike, lower prominence_frac / min_distance_deg and re-run the single global fit_pattern. 4) Accept when peak_region_r2 ≥ 0.90, all visible reflections modelled, and residual is structureless (small apex residual on the sharpest peaks is the irreducible split-PV limit — do not chase it). 5) Constraints: amplitude > 0, FWHM in [0.05°, 2.0°], eta in [0,1]. 6) Scherrer with instrumental_fwhm_deg=0.0 (unknown; flag sizes as lower-bound / upper-bound on broadening unless a LaB6/Si standard FWHM is supplied). W-H only if ≥5 peaks span sin θ range > 0.1. For the in-situ series, fix this single fit_range window and reuse auto-detection on every frame; expect lattice/cell to move with temperature — that peak-position drift is the physics of interest, not an error to suppress.
